column4: A multi-billion payment to the Fund falls due and reserves are not enough.
The economy minister: “Let us sign a new agreement. It is bitter, but it avoids default.”

column3: Pay with reserves and sign nothing
column4: The chief of staff: “We pay with what we have. We will not hand over our sovereignty.”
Unions demand raises above inflation. Employers say they cannot pay.
The labour minister: “Wages have been losing ground. Let us sign and avoid a strike.”
The economy minister: “If we approve this, inflation will never come down.”
Thousands of families occupy a plot on the outskirts of Buenos Aires. The owner demands immediate eviction.
The security minister: “Private property must be respected. We evict today.”
The social development minister: “Let us offer serviced plots. Nobody occupies land for fun.”
Teachers' unions announce an open-ended strike. The school year does not start.

column3: Raise teacher pay from national funds
column4: The education minister: “No teachers, no country. Let us put up the money.”
The chief of staff: “No work, no pay. The children must be in the classroom.”
Energy companies say they cannot invest without updated tariffs.
The energy secretary: “Either we pay for power or we sit in the dark.”
The chief of staff: “A tariff hike now would be political suicide.”
A New York court orders full payment to the funds that rejected the debt swap.
The economy minister: “Paying is expensive, but we get back into the markets.”
The chief of staff: “We will not pay the vultures what other creditors did not get.”
Rural associations announce a lockout and block highways against export duties.
The agriculture minister: “Without farmers there are no dollars. We have to listen.”
The economy minister: “We cannot give in to an employers' lockout.”
A British company announces oil exploration in waters off the islands.
The foreign minister: “It is our territory. We take the case to the United Nations.”
The deputy foreign minister: “We protest, but without burning bridges with London.”
The parallel dollar jumps 20% in a week and black-market exchange houses cannot keep up.
The central bank governor: “We must close the gap even if it hurts.”
The security minister: “We are going after the speculators.”
Drug gangs threaten the governor and attack shops. The city lives in fear.
The security minister: “We need the full power of the state.”
The attorney general: “Follow the money, not just the foot soldiers.”
The opposition passes a generous pension law. Do you veto it?
The economy minister: “There is no money. Fiscal balance is not negotiable.”
The chief of staff: “We cannot fight pensioners in an election year.”
A group of provincial governors make their votes in Congress conditional on public works and transfers.
The interior minister: “With the provinces' votes we get our laws through.”
The economy minister: “The political slush fund is over.”
Bus companies stop running: they say subsidies do not cover wages.
The transport secretary: “Millions cannot get to work.”
The economy minister: “Let fares reflect the real cost.”
An investor group offers to buy a big club if football clubs may become private companies.
The sports minister: “Clubs need capital to compete.”
The chief of staff: “We will not touch the heart of Argentine football.”

column3: Bill to repeal the abortion law
column4: Governing-party deputies propose repealing the law on voluntary termination of pregnancy.
The religious affairs secretary: “Let us defend life from conception.”
The women's affairs minister: “It is a right won on the streets.”
In December there are not enough pesos to pay the thirteenth-month bonus to state workers and pensioners.

column3: Ask the central bank for pesos
column4: The chief of staff: “We pay. We will deal with it later.”
The economy minister: “We will not print money. It will be paid in two instalments.”
Congress has passed increases for disability care providers and pensions.
The economy minister: “The surplus is untouchable. Let us first review the wrongly granted pensions.”
The chief of staff: “This political cost is not worth paying.”
After a huge march, Congress passes funds for universities and lecturers' salaries.
The chief of staff: “First the universities must accept audits.”
The education minister: “Public universities are a source of national pride.”
Residents at the country's main children's hospital strike over pay.
The health minister: “We cannot lose the country's best paediatricians.”
The economy minister: “If we give in here, everyone will ask tomorrow.”
Washington offers a huge swap line, but asks to limit China's presence in strategic infrastructure.
The foreign minister: “It is the backing we need to prevent a run.”
The economy minister: “China is our second trading partner. We cannot pick sides.”

column3: The dollar hits the band ceiling
column4: Pre-election pressure pushes the dollar to the top of the band.
The central bank governor: “The band will be defended. Our word is at stake.”

column3: Let it rise and widen the band
column4: The economy minister: “Let the market find its price.”
An investor group offers to buy the loss-making state airline.
The deregulation minister: “Let those who fly pay for it, not every Argentine.”
The chief of staff: “It connects provinces no private airline wants to serve.”
The governing party proposes suspending the open primaries to save money and simplify the election.
The interior minister: “It is a pointless expense voters do not want.”
The spokesman: “We will not change the rules months before a vote.”
A 15-year-old kills a shopkeeper in a robbery. The country debates lowering the age of criminal responsibility.
The security minister: “Whoever commits the crime pays for it, whatever their age.”
The human development minister: “Prison does not reform a 14-year-old.”

column3: Mining governors want the glacier law changed
column4: Andean provinces demand the law be relaxed to allow multi-billion copper projects.
The mining secretary: “Copper is the next Vaca Muerta.”
The environment secretary: “Water is worth more than copper.”
Argentines keep over 200 billion dollars outside the banking system. How do you lure them in?

column3: Let them be spent, no questions asked
column4: The economy minister: “Every dollar out of the mattress means investment and spending.”

column3: Require the source to be declared
column4: The anti-money-laundering chief: “We cannot become a laundromat.”
The austerity plan includes closing agricultural research stations in the provinces.
The deregulation minister: “Let those who benefit from research pay for it.”
The agriculture secretary: “Without the institute, small farmers are on their own.”

column3: The union federation offers to negotiate
column4: The labour federation promises no strikes if union dues and sector-wide agreements are kept.
The interior minister: “A reform with consensus lasts longer.”
The human capital minister: “Union privileges are over.”
Textile mills, metalworkers and appliance makers complain of unfair competition from imports.
The industry secretary: “Without industry there are no jobs.”
The economy minister: “Argentines deserve international prices.”
Kyiv asks Argentina for military equipment and support at the UN. Russia warns of trade reprisals.

column3: Send aid and vote with the West
column4: The foreign minister: “We stand on the side of freedom.”
The deputy foreign minister: “It is not our war.”

column3: UN vote on the Middle East
column4: The General Assembly votes on a ceasefire that Israel and the US reject.
The UN ambassador: “Civilian lives come first.”

column3: Vote with the US and Israel
column4: The foreign minister: “We are allies and we will show it.”
The government considers moving the Argentine embassy in Israel to Jerusalem.
The President: “It is a promise and we will keep it.”
The foreign minister: “Now is not the time: we would risk trade with Arab countries.”

column3: Thousands of migrants at the border
column4: Venezuelan families wait at the northern border without papers.
The human development minister: “Argentina has always been a land of immigrants.”
The security minister: “Argentines first.”

column3: The Chinese space station in Neuquén
column4: The US asks Argentina to review the agreement that lets China run a space antenna in Patagonia.
The defence minister: “No one operates on Argentine soil without oversight.”
The foreign minister: “China is our customer. Let us not break contracts.”
Washington asks Argentina to exclude Chinese suppliers from its 5G network.
The innovation secretary: “Network security is not negotiable.”
The economy minister: “May the best offer win.”
The Brazilian government proposes a common currency for Mercosur trade.
The foreign minister: “Trading without dollars saves reserves.”
The central bank governor: “We have enough trouble with one currency.”
There are two offers: used US fighters or newer, cheaper Chinese jets.
The air force chief: “It ties us to NATO as an ally.”
The economy minister: “They are newer and we pay in instalments.”
European farmers push to block Argentine beef over deforestation in the north.
The environment secretary: “It is a chance to stop forest clearing.”
The agriculture secretary: “It is protectionism dressed up as ecology.”
